gaps.sentence: Only after the third reminder ___ she reply to my email.
gaps.explanation: 'Only after' fronts the condition, so 'did she reply' inverts.

gaps.sentence: Among the guests ___ the ambassador and her staff.
gaps.hint: fronted 'among' — verb agrees with later subject
gaps.explanation: Among the guests were the ambassador and her staff — verb before subject.

gaps.sentence: Seldom have I been so ___ by a performance.
gaps.explanation: 'moved' — the audience was emotionally affected; inversion with have been.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the chances of success be improved by patience.
gaps.explanation: Little will the chances be improved… — inversion with future.

gaps.sentence: Nowhere ___ you find a better example of Gothic architecture.
Not until the second edition ___ the book become a bestseller.
gaps.explanation: 'Not until the second edition did the book become …'.

gaps.sentence: Under no circumstances ___ the door be left unlocked.
gaps.explanation: 'Under no circumstances should/must the door be left unlocked' — modal + inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not since the 1990s ___ unemployment been so low.
gaps.explanation: Not since X has Y happened — present perfect inversion.
